study_label: FUNCTION trial: tocilizumab with or without methotrexate in early rheumatoid arthritis

objective.value: To evaluate the clinical and radiographic efficacy and safety of tocilizumab (TCZ), in combination with methotrexate (MTX) and as monotherapy, in early rheumatoid arthritis.

population.value: Adults aged 18 years or older with moderate-to-severe active rheumatoid arthritis of no more than 2 years' duration, classified according to revised 1987 ACR criteria, with no previous MTX or biologic-agent treatment. Enrolled patients had poor-prognosis features, including DAS28-ESR >3.2, specified joint-count and inflammatory-marker criteria, and RF/anti-CCP positivity or erosions. Baseline RA duration was very early (mean 0.4-0.5 years).

intervention.value: Intravenous TCZ every 4 weeks in one of three regimens: 4 mg/kg TCZ plus MTX, 8 mg/kg TCZ plus MTX, or 8 mg/kg TCZ plus placebo. MTX/placebo started at 7.5 mg/week and could be increased to a maximum of 20 mg/week by week 8 in patients with ongoing swollen or tender joints.

comparator.value: Placebo plus MTX; placebo was administered intravenously every 4 weeks, and MTX was initiated at 7.5 mg/week with escalation to a maximum of 20 mg/week by week 8 as specified.

duration_follow_up.value: The trial was designed for 2 years; this report presents the primary analysis of the first 52 weeks. The primary endpoint was assessed at week 24, with results also reported through week 52.

primary_outcome.value: Proportion of patients achieving DAS28-ESR remission (DAS28-ESR <2.6) at week 24.

effect_result.value: The primary endpoint was met for 8 mg/kg TCZ plus MTX versus placebo plus MTX: DAS28-ESR remission at week 24 was 44.8% (130/290) versus 15.0% (43/287), OR 4.77 (95% CI 3.19-7.14), p<0.0001. At week 52, remission was 49.0% versus 19.5%, respectively. Week-24 remission was also higher versus placebo plus MTX with 4 mg/kg TCZ plus MTX (31.9% vs 15.0%; OR 2.72, 95% CI 1.80-4.11; p<0.0001) and 8 mg/kg TCZ monotherapy (38.7% vs 15.0%; OR 3.70, 95% CI 2.47-5.55; p<0.0001).

safety.value: Any adverse events/serious adverse events occurred in 88.3%/10.7% with 8 mg/kg TCZ plus MTX, 85.6%/8.6% with 8 mg/kg TCZ monotherapy, 88.6%/10.0% with 4 mg/kg TCZ plus MTX, and 83.3%/8.5% with placebo plus MTX. Adverse events causing premature withdrawal occurred in 20.3%, 11.6%, 12.1%, and 7.4%, respectively. Infections were the most frequently reported adverse events and serious adverse events. ALT elevations of grade 2 or higher occurred most frequently with TCZ plus MTX (15.6% with 4 mg/kg and 23.8% with 8 mg/kg), versus 8.2% with TCZ monotherapy and 8.5% with placebo plus MTX.

sample_size.analyzed: 1157 patients in the ITT population; 1153 patients in the safety population
